## Parent distribution pole theorem

For S_e(z)=N(e) Integral_K R(x,e) delta(z F(x)-G(x)) dx, pairing with phi gives
N(e) Integral_K R(x,e)/Abs[F(x)] phi(G/F) dx. The absolute-slope factor is essential.
For unit cuts this is the original scalar integral, not a numerator-compensated
moment. Require a fixed compact semialgebraic physical domain of dimension d,
bounded regulator-independent rational/algebraic map defined almost everywhere,
fixed algebraic density/branch/divisor/boundary data, affine epsilon exponents,
regular holomorphic factors, and equality to the prescribed physical integral
on a shared absolute-convergence domain, with all sheets/multiplicities retained.

Resolve the closure of the ACTUAL physical graph, not the entire equation
zF-G=0: F=G=x gives x(z-1)=0 with an extraneous vertical component. Graph closure
and its resolution preserve dimension d. Alternatively principalize (F,G):
F=u^nu f, G=u^nu g with f,g without a common zero. Boundedness of G/F on the
physical lift excludes f=0 on its closure, so g/f extends smoothly. Resolve
other divisors simultaneously. Retain the pullback of the original density,
not an induced Euclidean graph measure.

After resolution, each chart has Product[u_i^(A_i+B_i e)] H(u,e) phi(m(u)).
Each coordinate contributes at most one resonant Taylor denominator at e=0.
An uncancelled polar term with B_i=0 would contradict the common convergence
hypothesis. Smoothness on compact charts controls a finite set of test-function
seminorms. Thus pole order is <=d+p as a distribution when normalization has
pole order<=p; equivalently val >= val(N)-d. A proper regulator-independent
pushforward cannot increase pole order.

Primary mathematical inputs: Leon-Cardenal, Veys, Zuniga-Galindo,
https://arxiv.org/abs/1002.4589, Theorems1/2. This pushforward application is a
corollary of resolution and normal-crossing pole counting, not a verbatim
published phase-space theorem.

Four massless particles have six invariant pairs minus the scale constraint,

therefore permits -5 for the original distribution IF all above hypotheses,
including slope and causal convergence, are certified. No explicit resolution
